question: Write a postcard from a lighthouse keeper.
base_frame:
Q: Write a postcard from a lighthouse keeper.
A:

steered.text:
**[THE ST. CLEMENS LIGHTHOUSE]**
**[ISLE OF SKERRY, NORTH SEA]**
**[14th of November, 1892]**

My Dearest Elara,

The gale has finally broken. The sea is still churning like a black iron trough, and the great bell of this tower still rings out its warning to the *Hesperus*, but the wind has gone down to a mere moan.

I write this with hands that are not yet dry, for the salt water is a cruel master, and it has a way of finding the cracks in the mortar. I hope you are warm in London, though I tell you truly, the frost is already biting the eaves here. I have no fire to speak of but the one that feeds the oil lamp in the lantern room, and even that flame trembles when the moon is too low.

The seal below the pier is gone. He knew the winter was coming. I saw his ribs through the ice before he slipped beneath. Aye, aye, I say it every night when the shadow crosses the floorboards. "Gone to the deep, gone to the deep."

I dreamt of you last night, Elara. You stood in the doorway of the cottage, wearing that blue shawl you stole from my sister's chest, and you told me the foghorn sounded like a lover's sigh. I awoke with a start, for the foghorn does not sigh, and the keeper is a hard man, my heart, but the sea knows I am soft.

The lantern is full. The oil is fresh from the cask, smelling of iron and old pennies. I have scrubbed the glass until my knuckles were white. I shall climb up there at dawn, when the sun is a red coin in the cup of the sky, and I shall polish it one last time for your sake.

Come back to me, love. The boat is mended, and the tide will be high enough to carry you home by next month. Until then, I shall keep the light burning. I shall keep the bell ringing. I shall watch the foam until my eyes go blind.

Kiss the frost for me. It is the only thing left that is clean.

Yours, in the salt and the dark,

**Barnaby**

*(P.S.

plain.text:
**[Back of Card - Handwritten Address]**
123 Maple Drive
Portland, OR 97205
USA

**[Front of Card - Scenic View]**
*A view of the crashing waves against the granite base of the tower, with the lantern room glowing warmly at the top against a twilight sky.*

**[Inside Message]**

Dearest Elias,

The fog rolled in thick this morning, turning the sea into a gray mirror. I lit the beacon an hour ago, and watching the beam cut through the mist is the only comfort I need. The wind is howling up here, rattling the gears of the clockwork mechanism, but the light holds steady.

We caught a school of mackerel near the reef today; they must have been confused by the shifting currents. It makes me think of your fishing trips back home. The isolation up here is strange—sometimes I forget the days pass, other times I count the incoming tide schedules until my hands ache.

I miss the smell of your coffee and the sound of the rain on a tin roof. Here, the only sound is the eternal crash of the surf. But tonight, as the moon rises, the water looks like liquid silver, and the horizon seems endless.

Stay warm and safe. Write soon so I can read your words by lamplight.

With love and a steady light,

**Arthur**
*Keeper of the Blackwood Point Light*
*Oct 14th*
